brief.headline: Memory Rally Intact: HBM4 Price Doubling, Temasek Stake Sparks 5-7% Pop
brief.summary: <cite index="1-2">HBM4 pricing projected at $31-32/GB, nearly double HBM3e's $17-18/GB</cite>, with <cite index="1-14">Samsung Q3 HBM4 revenue expected to more than triple QoQ</cite>. <cite index="1-11">TrendForce forecasts conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3, NAND Flash prices up 10-15%</cite>, decelerating from Q2's ~60% jumps but still elevated. <cite index="40-1,40-4">Samsung closed up 6.7% and SK Hynix up 5.5%</cite> Wednesday after <cite index="39-13">Asia Business Daily reported Temasek plans direct investment in both chipmakers</cite>. <cite index="19-6">US hyperscalers plan $660-690B infrastructure capex in 2026, vast majority directed at AI compute</cite>, with <cite index="19-7">all hyperscalers reporting supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained markets</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Samsung outperforming SK Hynix on HBM4 ramp velocity (Q3 revenue tripling vs. SK's unspecified trajectory) and higher Q2 ASP gains (mid-40% DRAM, high-60% NAND vs. SK's 30% DRAM, mid-50% NAND). SK retains structural share lead at 50-55% HBM market share but facing speculation around LTA pricing pressure. Temasek news lifts both equally near-term but Samsung's Device Solutions diversification (memory + logic) offers better downside cushion if consumer DRAM weakens. Watch for SK Hynix labor negotiation updates (referenced in search results) as potential production risk offset. Tactical long Samsung vs. SK Hynix into Q3 earnings on HBM4 delta.

memory_cycle.notes: Q3 contract pricing still rising 13-18% DRAM, 10-15% NAND but materially slower than Q2's 58-63% pace. Spot markets showing fatigue: DDR4 +0.93% weekly, transaction volumes shrinking. Structural shortage persists (wafer capacity redirected to HBM, no relief until late 2027/2028 new fabs). Consumers hitting affordability ceiling but hyperscaler LTAs locking in floor pricing. Pricing power rotating from conventional DRAM to HBM as DDR5 margins (>80%) force suppliers to demand premium HBM pricing. Cycle likely extends into 2027 on AI infrastructure capex but rate-of-change inflection already visible.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-3">HBM4 prices expected to surge to $4-5/Gb in 2027, up from ~$2 in 2H26</cite>, driven by <cite index="2-4,2-5">4-6 month production cycles, lower initial yields, and 3x wafer capacity consumption vs. DDR5</cite>. <cite index="4-15">HBM3 ~$200/stack (24GB), HBM3E ~$300/stack (36GB), HBM4 ~$500/stack (48GB)</cite> as of August. <cite index="4-3,4-9">Supply remains constrained through 2026</cite>, with <cite index="4-11">HBM3E lead times at 20-26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="2-6,2-7">Majors locking up supply via 3-5 year LTAs; booming DDR5 margins (>80%) forcing premium HBM pricing just to justify line shifts</cite>. <cite index="32-7,32-8">Micron has multi-year supply agreements allocating DRAM and HBM to customers several generations ahead, illustrating why increased CoWoS capacity doesn't automatically translate to higher AI chip output</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: HBM4 pricing could hit $31-32/GB, double HBM3e; Samsung Q3 HBM4 revenue to triple QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Samsung Device Solutions HBM4 ramp accelerating faster than consensus; supports H2 revenue mix shift and validates >60% HBM4 share of total HBM sales guide. Reinforces pricing power into 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Temasek plans direct investment in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix
news_pulse.implication: First direct Temasek exposure to Korean equities; $401B AUM sovereign whale validates memory cycle durability. Lifted both stocks 5-7% Wednesday; technical overhang cleared post-July selloff.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS yield hits 98-99% in HVM; supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing (130K wafers/month target) but TSMC flagging HBM and ABF substrates as new constraints. Positive for Samsung/SK as CoWoS availability no longer limits HBM shipments, but memory supply tightness shifts leverage to them.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 DRAM contract pricing +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ (vs. Q2's ~60% jumps)
news_pulse.implication: Deceleration confirms consumer affordability ceiling hit, not supply improvement. Still strong double-digit gains; hyperscaler LTAs with floor pricing lock in structural upside into 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler AI capex guidance $660-690B for 2026, up 81% YoY; supply-constrained not demand-constrained
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+. Capex wall de-risks HBM demand; 75% allocated to GPUs/HBM/servers. No signs of slowdown despite ROI scrutiny.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM spot trading subdued; DDR4 1Gx8 3200MT/s up 0.93% to $42.50 (Aug 10)
news_pulse.implication: Spot momentum fading; buyers resisting incremental increases. Contract prices still climbing but spot stagnation historically leads TrendForce to trim later-quarter forecasts. Monitor for Q4 guide cuts.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI enters bull market; Samsung +4%, SK Hynix +7% on memory stock rotation
news_pulse.implication: Memory outperforming broader tech for first time since June per Fundstrat. Technical rebound from July lows confirmed; risk appetite returning to AI hardware names.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity 120K-140K wafers in 2026; NVIDIA secures ~60% allocation
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS fully booked 2026; top-3 customers (NVDA, Broadcom, AMD) lock >85%. Packaging no longer primary bottleneck but memory and ABF substrates emerging as next constraints per TSMC OCP comments.

brief.derivatives_signal: No options data in payload; ADR flow skewed bullish post-Temasek headline (HXSCL OTC +7% sympathy). KOSPI 200 futures likely front-running Samsung/SK weighting; monitor Index arb pressure if ADR premiums widen vs. KRX close. Volatility surface likely compressing after July drawdown; calendar spreads favoring front-month into September earnings. Watch USD/KRW; stronger won = FX headwind to translated earnings but historically correlates with foreign inflows to memory names.
